name: Dynamic Tags for Elementor – ACF, WooCommerce & Custom Fields
author: wowDevs

sections.description:
Dynamic Tags for Elementor adds 77 dynamic tags to the free Elementor editor, so a widget can show live WordPress data instead of text you typed by hand.

Type a heading once and it says the same thing on every page. A dynamic tag reads the value instead: the post title, the author’s name, a custom field, an ACF field, a WooCommerce product price. Change the data in WordPress and every page that uses the tag follows.

Click the dynamic tags icon on any text, link or image control, pick a source, and the widget is connected. It works with the widgets you already use (Heading, Text Editor, Button, Image and any other widget whose controls support dynamic content), and it does not require Elementor Pro.

What you can build with dynamic content

  • Blog post layouts. Post title, featured image, excerpt, publish date, categories and tags, comment count, and previous/next post links.
  • Author boxes. Author name, avatar, user meta and a link to the author archive.
  • Archive and category headers. Archive title, archive description, term description, term count and term meta.
  • Search results pages. The search query and the number of results found.
  • WooCommerce product layouts. Product title, price, sale badge, SKU, stock, rating, attributes, gallery images and an add-to-cart link.
  • Custom field driven pages. ACF fields, post custom fields, term meta and user meta, shown as text, links or images.
  • Site-wide details. Site title, tagline, site logo, the current year in a footer, and a login/logout link.

Controls on every tag

  • Fallback. What to show when the value is empty, so a missing excerpt never leaves a hole in the layout.
  • Before and After. Wrap the value in text without touching the widget: Posted on, min read.
  • Word limit. Trim long content to a set number of words.
  • Current or specific source. Read the post being viewed, or search and select one particular post, term, user or product.

All 77 dynamic tags

Post tags. Post title, ID, slug, date, time, author, comments count, excerpt, content, terms, status, type, custom field, featured image.

Site tags. Site title, tagline, current date and time, request parameter, shortcode.

Archive tags. Archive title, description, meta.

Term tags. Term ID, title, description, slug, count, meta.

User tags. User info, user meta, user avatar.

Search tags. Search query, search results count.

URL tags. Post URL, post terms URL, author URL, comments URL, featured image URL, post navigation URL, archive URL, site URL, term URL, user URL, login/logout URL, attachment URL.

Image tags. Featured image, author avatar, custom field image, archive meta image, site logo, site icon, user avatar.

WooCommerce dynamic tags

When WooCommerce is active, a WooCommerce group appears in the tag list:

  • Product data. Title, description, price, sale, SKU, stock, rating, shipping, type, attribute, terms, purchase note.
  • Product links. Product URL, add to cart URL, review URL, checkout URL, back to shop URL, product archive URL, product term URL, product term archive URL.
  • Product images. Featured image, gallery image, product term image.

Use them on the current product or pick a specific product by name, which makes it possible to feature one product on a landing page built with standard Elementor widgets.

ACF dynamic tags

When Advanced Custom Fields is active, an ACF group appears with five tags: ACF text, ACF URL, ACF image, ACF gallery and ACF date and time. Pick the field from a list and its value fills the control, with the same Fallback, Before and After options as every other text tag.

No ACF? The Post Custom Field, Custom Field Image, Term Meta, User Meta and Archive Meta tags read standard WordPress meta directly.

Lightweight by design

  • No front-end CSS or JavaScript. A dynamic tag renders inside someone else’s widget, so it adds no request to the page. The one script this plugin ships runs in the editor only.
  • WooCommerce and ACF tags load only when those plugins are active. Nothing is registered for a site that does not use them.
  • Works with free Elementor. Elementor Pro is not required.
  • No duplicate registration. If another active plugin already provides these same tags, this plugin steps aside, so a tag is never registered twice.

How to use a dynamic tag in Elementor

  1. Edit a page or template with Elementor and select a widget.
  2. Hover a text, link or image control and click the dynamic tags icon.
  3. Choose a tag from the list, for example Post Title.
  4. Click the tag name to open its settings: source, Fallback, Before, After and Word limit.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate Elementor, if it is not already.
  2. In WordPress, go to Plugins > Add New, search for “Dynamic Tags for Elementor”, then install and activate it. Or upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  3. Open any page in Elementor and click the dynamic tags icon on a text, link or image control.

There is no settings page. The tags are available as soon as the plugin is active.
sections.faq:
What is a dynamic tag in Elementor?

A dynamic tag connects a widget control to a piece of WordPress data. Instead of typing a value, you choose where it comes from, such as the post title or a custom field, and Elementor fills it in when the page is rendered.

Do I need Elementor Pro to use dynamic tags?

No. This plugin adds its dynamic tags to free Elementor, version 3.5 or newer.

How do I show an ACF field in Elementor?

Activate Advanced Custom Fields, click the dynamic tags icon on a control and choose an ACF tag: text, URL, image, gallery, or date and time. Then select the field in the tag settings.

How do I show a WooCommerce product price in an Elementor widget?

Activate WooCommerce, click the dynamic tags icon on a text control such as a Heading, and choose Product Price. You can show the regular price, the sale price, both, or the discount, for the current product or one you select.

Can I show custom fields without ACF?

Yes. The Post Custom Field, Custom Field Image, Term Meta, User Meta and Archive Meta tags read standard WordPress meta.

Can a tag show data from a specific post instead of the current one?

Yes. Post, term, user and product tags can read the current item or one you search for and select by name.

What happens when a dynamic value is empty?

Text tags have a Fallback setting. Whatever you enter there is shown when the source has no value.

Why can’t I see the WooCommerce or ACF tags?

Those groups are registered only while WooCommerce or Advanced Custom Fields is active. Activate the plugin and reload the editor.

Will it slow my site down?

It adds no stylesheet and no front-end script. The only asset is an editor-only control, loaded while you are building.

Does it work with other page builders or the block editor?

No. Dynamic tags are an Elementor feature and render inside Elementor widgets.
sections.changelog:
1.0.2 [15th November 2026]

  • Fixed: Site crash on sites with many users caused by User Avatar dynamic tag.
  • Fixed: Search & Select controls running unlimited queries when loading saved selections.
  • Improved: Lighter term queries in Search & Select controls & Product Term Archive URL tag.

1.0.1

  • First release: 77 dynamic tags across post, site, archive, term, user, search, URL, image, WooCommerce and ACF groups.
  • Fallback, Before, After and word-limit controls on text tags.
  • Search-and-select source for post, term, user and product tags.
  • WooCommerce and ACF groups registered conditionally.

screenshots.caption: Click the dynamic tags icon next to any Elementor control and pick a tag — here, Post Title for a Heading.
The Heading now shows the post's real title. Change the title in WordPress and the page follows.
Every text tag has Before, After and Fallback; most add a Word Limit. The result shows live in the editor.
Show a specific post instead of the current one: switch to Selected Post and search by name.
Image controls get their own tags: featured image, author avatar, site logo, user avatar and more.
WooCommerce tags: pick a product and show its price — regular, sale, both or the discount.
ACF tags read your custom fields. Here a "Distance" text field fills part of the post meta line.
What visitors see: title, category, author, date, ACF field, featured image, excerpt and product price — all filled in by tags.
